technical-data.invention-title: METHOD IN AN INFORMATION SERVICE FOR A MOBILE PHONE
PROCEDE APPLIQUE DANS UN SERVICE D'INFORMATION ET CONCERNANT UN TELEPHONE MOBILE

abstract.p: The present invention relates to a method for use in an information service provided to a mobile terminal subscriber, the method comprising the steps of receiving and gathering information to an information server (8) from different sources such as information producers (15) or the customer's corporate body (14) or other group of association, compiling selectively from the gathered information an information package to be disseminated specifically to the customer and transmitting the information package to the customer's mobile terminal subscription (1). The information is selected on the basis of an information service need profile generated for the customer or, respectively, a customer group, whereby the service need profile itself is based on customer-submitted information, data related to the customer's mobile terminal subscription including terminal position data, call transfer and other optional settings or terminal accessibility history, as well as information possibly submitted by the customer's groups of association including vacation times, job description or travel times and/or other data. The method is particularly suited for use in conjunction with the WAP (Wireless Application Protocol) technology.

L'invention concerne un procédé conçu pour être mis en application dans un service d'information fourni à un abonné mobile et consistant à recevoir et à rassembler des informations destinées à un serveur d'information (8) et émanant de différentes sources, telles que des producteurs d'information (15), la société (14) du client ou d'autres groupes d'associations, à compiler de façon sélective à partir des informations rassemblées, un ensemble d'informations à disséminer de manière spécifique à l'intention du client et à transmettre cet ensemble d'informations à l'abonnement mobile (1) du client. Les informations sont sélectionnées sur la base d'un profil de besoins de services d'informations généré pour le client ou un groupe de clients, ce profil étant basé sur les informations soumises par le client, sur les données concernant l'abonnement du client à un terminal téléphonique mobile, y compris les données de position de ce terminal, le transfert d'appel et d'autres précisions éventuelles ou un historique d'accessibilité au terminal, ainsi que sur les informations éventuellement soumises par les groupes d'associations du client, y compris les périodes de vacances, la description du poste ou les périodes de déplacement et/ou d'autres données. Ce procédé est particulièrement applicable avec la technologie du WAP (protocole d'application sans fil).

description.p: METHOD IN AN INFORMATION SERVICE FOR A MOBILE PHONE

The invention relates to a method suited for submitting information to a mobile terminal subscriber automatically on the basis of predetermined subscriber needs without receiving a distinct order for information from the subscriber immediately prior to the transmission of information.

This kind of method is used for providing personalized information service to a mobile terminal subscriber, whereby in the method the information is transmitted to a mobile phone or any other mobile terminal using the GSM (Global System for Mobile Communications) technology or other telecommunications means. The service may be provided to an individual mobile terminal subscriber as well as to an entire group of mobile terminal subscribers formed by, e.g., the personnel of a corporate body.

The prior-art technology is based on methods, wherein the mobile terminal subscriber first sends a request according to a predetermined procedure which triggers a search on the needed information that is then transmitted to the mobile terminal subscriber. In practice, this takes place so that the mobile terminal subscriber sends a short message in the SMS format with the request for desired information to a telephone number given by the service provider. In a short while, the mobile terminal subscriber will receive a short message in the SMS format with the requested information. This embodiment is technically based on a server operating in conjunction with the SMS exchange that receives the SMS-type short message indicating the need for certain information and retrieves over the telecommunications network the desired information, compiles the same into the SMS-type short message of an appropriate content and sends it to the mobile terminal subscriber requesting the information.

Also Internet pages can be read by means of certain mobile phone models.
The state-of-the-art technology is capable of facilitating the use of subscriber services that are more advanced and user-friendly than those outlined above. For instance, the so-called WAP (Wireless Application Protocol) technology permits mobile phones to receive information also in graphic format. With the help of the WAP technology, it is possible to connect mobile phone networks to the Internet, whereby a mobile terminal in practice becomes an Internet browser. A prerequisite to this is that the Internet pages are compiled using the WML (Wireless Markup Language) code instead of the conventional HTML code. The WML code was developed for efficient transmission of graphic information over the limited transmission bandwidth of the mobile phone network. With the help of the WAP technology, also the user interfaces of information services may be developed toward greater user- friendliness, whereby a mobile terminal subscriber may replace the tedious task of sending a standard-format request from his mobile terminal by a selection of the desired service from his graphic user interface. By virtue of the WAP technology, also a data transfer call can be used for transmitting information in the WML-coded format instead of passing the information superimposed on an SMS-type short message.

There are also short-message services available that are based on information bulletins distributed at regular intervals as SMS-type transmissions. The selection of these services cover a wide spectrum of different areas of interest wherefrom the customer can choose his favorite one(s). In addition to the standard scheduled bulletins, special announcements can be broadcast if any unusually important news emerge within the scope of the service. Such areas of interest may be categorized as, e.g., news, business news, sports news or weather forecasts.

In the art are also known methods that allow information to be sent to the service customer terminal according to predetermined personalized user profile. These kinds of methods are described in patent publications WO 98/51097 and WO 97/41654. In the method disclosed in patent publication WO 97/41654, the retrieved information can be sent to the service customer's mobile terminal. The scope of patent publica-
tion WO 98/51097 covers a more general selection of different services that can be implemented over a communications connection established between a mobile terminal and a service provider.

A problem hampering the prior-art technologys in the viewpoint of the mobile terminal subscriber is the lack of an autonomous initiative from the side of the offered information services. To obtain information, the mobile terminal subscriber must always submit a request message. If the mobile terminal subscriber wishes to get information on changes in certain news groups or selected areas of interest, he must send every now and then a request message to receive updated information.

From the standpoint of the mobile terminal subscriber, this is an awkward as well as inefficient situation inasmuch the information on an already occurred change is submitted only on request instead of being transmitted immediately in real time with the occurrence of the change. If the mobile terminal subscriber wishes to minimize the delay caused by this, he must resort to continually sending update requests. The lack of an autonomous initiative in the function of prior-art information services also occurs such that the mobile terminal subscriber cannot access an information service of the WAP technology type involving a data call connection immediately when it is available, but rather not until the calling mobile terminal subscriber has himself actively established a data call connection.

Another problem experienced by the mobile terminal subscriber is the complicated control of the offered service. If the mobile terminal subscriber wishes to use certain information services or certain types of information services, he must know a priori exactly the types of requests that must be sent in order to access the desired information. This is awkward to the mobile terminal subscriber particularly if the number of services the subscriber wishes to access is large. While the graphic user interfaces based on the WAP technology can bring some ease to the control of offered information services, they cannot entirely remove the problem.

One handicap is the small number of Internet home pages accessible in the WML format. Even if the service provider accessed by a mobile terminal subscriber could
convert an HTML-coded Internet home page into the WML format when so requested by the mobile terminal subscriber, the operation may take an unbearably long time in order to represent an efficient customer service feature. Obviously, WML-coded home pages will probably become more common with time, but the transition period can be long.

Information bulletin services in turn are hampered by the wide scope of subject areas. An information bulletin service can be compared with a newspaper or periodical inasmuch the subscriber reads only the articles which interest him. Because of the small size of mobile phone displays, even topics of relatively narrow scope are clumsy to assess via an information bulletin service, since even a major portion of the bulletins may be of minor interest value to the subscriber even if he might be attracted to the subject in general. If a large selection of topics is offered, it is possible that the subscriber finds a news group with a content predominantly interesting to him. On the other hand, a large selection poses the dilemma of a good choice. Yet, some individual subscriber may fail to find a suitable news group even from the largest selection.

It is an object of the invention to anticipate the information service needs of a mobile terminal subscriber both qualitatively and quantitatively. In part, the service needs are estimated on the basis of user data submitted earlier by the subscriber in regard to such items as work profile, hobbies, subjects of interest or weekly/daily routines and, in part, complemented by other available data associated with the mobile terminal subscriber. Such complementary data may be, e.g., position information of the mobile terminal, unaccessibility of the mobile terminal or a location thereof outside the range of reach for a given time, call transfers or barring of incoming calls activated by the mobile terminal subscriber, or further, vacation times, leaves of sickness, work travel times or other information submitted by the mobile terminal subscriber's association group such as his employer, corporate body or association. Ultimately, however, the mobile terminal subscriber is the party that defines which pieces of information shall be valid in the tailoring of an information service for his needs. In the case that the customer is a mobile terminal subscriber group, such as the
personnel of a corporate body, the information service can be profiled separately for each member of the group or collectively for the entire group. Utilizing the estimated information service needs, the provider of the information service selects from the available wealth of information those up-to-date pieces of information that are most relevant for the customer and then sends this selected information to the customer on an autonomous initiative. Hence, information will be sent every time the information service provider finds transmission thereof appropriate. According to the invention, a command in the form of a short message or a number thereof to set up a data communications call is sent to the mobile terminal. After receiving the data communications call set-up command, the mobile terminal places a call to a determined network address, whereby a data communications connection is automatically established between the information server and the mobile terminal.
More specifically, the method according to the invention for use in an information service is characterized by what is stated in the characterizing part of claim 1.
The invention provides significant benefits.

By virtue of the invention, it is possible to implement an information service capable of submitting a customer substantial amounts of information contents automatically without any need to burden the customer with actions to actively search for the information. The transmission of large information contents is facilitated by the data communications connection established in the method. As the method deviates from known technologys by permitting the data communications connection to be established by way of a connection set-up command, the service can be automated and yet the data transfer can be charged according to normal billing rules to the customer subject to the call.

This kind of approach shifts a large portion of the information retrieval task and browsing of offered information from the customer over to the information service provider, which is experienced by the customer as an improved service level. Additionally, the customer does not need to memorize routines for retrieving desired
information.

The delay caused by the HTML-to-WML conversion in the browsing of Internet home pages can be eliminated to some extent inasmuch the method permits antici- pation of customer interests, whereby home pages of probable interest to the customers can be retrieved and converted in advance. Accordingly, the mobile phone service provider selects a group of home pages to be requested at a high probability, converts their contents into the WML-coded format and stores them in his own database, wherefrom they can be rapidly retrieved for use by the mobile terminal subscriber requesting them. If the mobile phone service provider can assume that the customer has an immediate need for gaining access to the information recently converted into the WML-coded format, the information can be transmitted to the customer immediately after the conversion step.

An information service configured according to the invention solves the problems associated with bulletin services by way of personalized tailoring of the information retrieval. Resultingly, the customer need not select the items of interests, but rather, a personal group of interest items is tailored to the customer.

The invention facilitates an individually tailored information service, wherein a mobile terminal subscriber will automatically receive information that with a high probability is of interest to him or serves his needs to a highly probable extent. Data transfer becomes faster and more efficient, since the mobile terminal subscriber will receive information at the earliest possible instant on which the information is available. The information service will be seen by the customer operating at an improved level and with greater user-friendliness, since a substantially shorter time is needed for retrieving the information, while the discarding of irrelevant information takes an appreciably shorter time. On one hand, the goal is to provide the customer with all the necessary information for his needs and, on the other hand, to avoid transmission of unnecessary information to the customer, simultaneously paying attention to the changing needs of the customer.
The invention makes it possible to centralize and enhance the internal information distribution of a corporate body or association the reception of the external information flows that come to the corporate body or association. The implementation of the internal information distribution can be merged with the dissemination of general information by way of submitting the desired internal information to the information service provider. Then, the responsibility of screening and distributing the internal information is handed over to the service provider. Resultingly, burden of the internal information distribution imposed on the resources of a corporate body or association is eased and the internal information distribution will be available to an employee even when he is inaccessible by the conventional internal information distribution system, e.g., when being on a travel.

In the following, the invention will be described in more detail with the help of an example by making reference to the appended drawings. In the example, the method is divided into three submethods that in combination outline an exemplifying embodiment of the invention. The submethods are illustrated in FIGS. 1 - 3.

For full appreciation of the benefits of the invention, a situation is described in the example having the mobile terminal subscription of the mobile terminal subscriber located in some other country than the national country of the subscriber's local mobile phone network operator. Herein, the national country of the mobile phone operator is defined as the country within the borders of which the mobile phone operator can offer mobile terminal services utilizing the resources of the operator's local network, that is, without resorting to the mobile phone network and/or services of a third party operator. Further in the example, the term national mobile phone network operator is used when reference is made to a mobile phone network operator that provides services directly to a mobile terminal subscriber while, respectively, the term foreign mobile phone network operator is used when reference is made to a mobile phone network operator that in turn provides services to the national mobile phone network operator. Obviously, the invention can be implemented equally well when the mobile terminal of the mobile terminal subscriber is located in the national country of the mobile phone network operator.
For greater clarity, some specific details are omitted in the example from the functional description of a digital telephone network such as a GSM or UMTS (Universal Mobile Telecommunication System) network. In the case that the invention is implemented in a GSM network, the overall configuration includes a plurality of network components, whose function is not specifically mentioned in the description of the exemplifying embodiment, such components are a GMSC (Gateway Mobile Switching Center), a BSC (Base Station Controller) and a BSS (Base Station System), for example. The description also omits the possible acknowledge routines of the short-messages communications involved.

Accordingly, FIG. 1 is a schematic block diagram of the update routines of mobile terminal status and position data, setting of optional services and transmission of these data to an information server;
FIG. 2 is a schematic block diagram of the information flow processing performed by the mobile terminal subscriber, the mobile phone network operator or the information service provider; and

FIG. 3 is a schematic block diagram of the information selection performed on the raw information submitted by information producers so that the estimated needs of the mobile terminal subscriber are taken into account and then transmitting the selected information to the mobile terminal subscriber.

Referring to FIG. 1, the system shown therein comprises a foreign operator's MSC (Mobile Switching Center) 2a, a NLR (visitor location register) 2b operating in conjunction with the MSC 2a, a foreign operator's international exchange 3, a mobile terminal subscription 1 located within the coverage area of the MSC 2a, a national operator's international exchange 5, an international digital telephone network 4 connecting the international exchanges 3 and 5, a national operator's MSC 6, a national operator's HLR (home location register) 7 and an information server 8.
The optional services mentioned above to operate in conjunction with the mobile terminal subscription may comprise call transfer services or barring of incoming or outgoing calls. The term position information is used when reference is made both to the geographical position of the mobile terminal that may be given with the resolu- tion of the present country and possibly defined down to a more accurate position of the mobile terminal and its location within the mobile phone network. The position data may also define the foreign operator in whose network the terminal is roaming.

In the operation of the method illustrated in FIG. 1 for updating the status and loca- tion data of a mobile terminal subscription, also when the mobile terminal subscriber activates new services and submits data related thereto to the information server, the following steps are carried out:

101) A mobile terminal subscription 1 located abroad performs a position information update that occurs in conjunction with the log-in or log-out of the mobile phone to the network or when roaming into a new network or when additional services are set up via the foreign operator's MSC 2a in the visitor location register VLR 2b.

102) The visitor location register VLR 2b sends information on the subscriber's location update or setting-up of new services via the signaling channel to an appropriate international exchange 3 of the foreign operator.
103) and 104) The international exchange 3 sends the information via the international digital telephone network 4 to the national mobile phone network operator's international exchange 5.
105) The international exchange 5 sends the information to the national operator's MSC 6.

106) The national operator's MSC 6 sends the information to the home location register HLR 7.
107) The home location register HLR 7 sends the information to the information server 8 that stores the information.

Now referring to FIG. 2, the system shown therein comprises in a similar manner as the one shown in FIG. 1 a foreign operator's MSC 2 and a national operator's MSC 6, a foreign operator's international exchange 3 and a national operator's international exchange 5, a mobile terminal subscription 1, an international digital telephone network 4 and an information server 8. In addition to these, the system shown in FIG. 2 includes an SMS-type short-message exchange 9, a gateway server 10, a national operator's control connection 11, an information service provider's control connection 13 and an information network 12 over which the service provider's control connection 13 communicates with the information server 8.

The information flow associated with the mobile terminal subscription can be controlled in three different ways: by sending a service modification request from the mobile terminal subscription (steps 201-209 below), by modifying the information flow from the operator's control connection (step 210) or by modifying the information flow from the service provider's control connection over an information network such as the Internet (step 211).

The mobile terminal subscription can send the information flow modification request either as a single short message or, alternatively, using a plurality of the SMS-type short messages or a data connection call. Hence, the items illustrated in FIG. 2 include either steps 206a and 207a or, respectively, step 208b, depending on whether the modification request is sent in the SMS format or in the data connection call format. If the modification request is sent in the SMS format, steps 206a and 207a are carried out. Respectively, if the modification request is sent in the data connection call format, step 208b is carried out.

In the operation of the method illustrated in FIG. 2, the following steps are carried out during the modification of the information flow to the mobile terminal
subscriber:

201) A mobile terminal subscriber modifies the information flow of his interest using a WAP-based user interface, whereupon the mobile terminal subscription 1 sends a modification request to a foreign operator's MSC 2.
The modification request can be submitted either in an SMS-type short- message call or as a data connection call.
202) The MSC 2 sends the modification request via the signaling channel to an appropriate international exchange 3 of the foreign operator.
203) and 204) The international exchange 3 sends the modification request via the international digital telephone network 4 to the national mobile phone network operator's international exchange 5.
205) The international exchange 5 sends the modification request to the national operator's MSC 6.
206a) If the modification request is received by the MSC 6 as an SMS-type short message, the MSC 6 sends the modification request to a short-message service exchange 9.
207a) The SMS exchange 9 sends the modification request received as an SMS- type short message to a gateway server 10.
208a) If the modification request is received as a data connection call at the MSC 6, the MSC 6 sends the modification request directly to a gateway server 10.

209) The gateway server 10 sends the modification request to an information server 8. The information server stores the information and modifies in the desired manner the information flow transmitted to the mobile terminal subscription 1.
210) The modification command is sent from the network operator's control connection 11 to the information server 8. The information server stores the information and modifies in the desired manner the information flow transmitted to the mobile terminal subscription 1.

211) The modification command is sent from the information service provider's control connection 13 over the information network 12 to the information server 8. The information server stores the information and modifies in the desired manner the information flow transmitted to the mobile terminal subscription 1.

Now referring to FIG. 3, the system shown therein comprises in a similar manner as the one shown in FIG. 1 a foreign operator's MSC 2a, a VLR (visitor location register) 2b operating in conjunction with the MSC 2a, a foreign operator's international exchange 3, a mobile terminal subscription 1 located within the coverage area of the MSC 2a, a national operator's international exchange 5, an international digital telephone network 4 connecting the international exchanges 3 and 5, a national operator's MSC 6, a national operator's home location register HLR 7 and an information server 8. In addition to these, the system shown in FIG. 3 includes an SMS-type short-message exchange 9, a gateway server 10, an information system 14 of the user or user group corporate body and information providers 15.

The information providers may be such parties as Internet home page hosts, news agencies or other information service producers including transportation companies, stock exchanges and weather forecasting associations, for example.

To the information flow to be transmitted to the mobile terminal subscriber, information is selected from the information offered by the information producers and, optionally, also from information accessible in the information system of the corporate body with which the mobile terminal subscriber is associated. As a certain piece of information may be submitted to the information server via both of the
above-mentioned routes or from a plurality of information producers, the information server must be capable of selectively discarding redundant and already earlier to the mobile terminal subscriber transmitted information during the screening of the information to be transmitted to the mobile terminal subscriber. To the information to be sent to the mobile terminal subscriber may also be selected a portion of a larger information content, for example, the time tables of a transportation company can be searched for given routes over a given period of time.

In the description of the exemplifying embodiment, the information content screened for the use of the mobile terminal subscriber is called an information package. The information package screened for sending to the mobile terminal subscriber is transmitted to the mobile terminal subscriber formatted in the WML, either as an SMS- type short message or a data connection call depending on the size of the information package. Typically, the information package is transmitted as a single SMS-type short message or, if necessary, by sending a plurality of short messages. When the amount of data in the information package is substantial, the mobile terminal is controlled with the help of an SMS-type short message to set up for a data connection call. After receiving the control command for setting up a data connection call, the mobile terminal automatically establishes a data connection call to the informa- tion server that then transmits the information package over the data connection call. Hence, only the steps numbered as 314 - 320 in the following exemplifying embodiment need to be carried out when a data connection call is used for transmission.

The transmission of information packages may be optionally complemented with a feedback query function, whereby the customer can express his sentiments about the transmitted information package. Then, on the basis of the received feedback, the information flow transmitted to the customer can be modified as required.

In the operation of the method illustrated in FIG. 3 for selective sorting of the information received from information producers and transmitting the thus selected information to a mobile terminal subscription, the following steps are carried out:
301) An information server 8 retrieves or receives information from information producers 15 and compares the content of the thus obtained information with the anticipated information service need profile of the mobile terminal subscriber.

302) The information server 8 retrieves or receives information from the corporate information system 14 and compares the content of the thus obtained information with the anticipated information service need profile of the mobile terminal subscriber.

303) The information server 8 selectively sorts the received information to compile the information package to be send to the mobile terminal subscriber, converts the information content into the WML-coded format if necessary and sends the information package thus processed to a gateway server 10.

304) Depending on the size of the information package, the gateway server 10 either sends the information package directly as an SMS-type short message or, alternatively, issues a data connection call set-up command to a short- message service exchange SMS 9.
305) The short-message service exchange SMS 9 relays the information package or, respectively, the data connection call set-up command to a MSC 6.
306) The MSC 6 sends a query to the home location register HLR 7 in order to find the so-called roaming number of the mobile terminal subscription 1.
With the help of the roaming number, the information package or, respectively, the data connection call set-up command can be routed to the mobile terminal subscription 1.

307) The home location register HLR 7 sends a query to the visitor location register VLR 2b that is indicated to have the mobile terminal subscription 1 within its coverage area. After the receipt of the query, the visitor location
register 2b sends the requested roaming number as a reply to the home location register HLR 7.
308) The home location register HLR 7 relays the roaming number of the mobile terminal subscription 1 to the MSC 6.

309) Based on the roaming number of the mobile terminal subscription 1 , the MSC 6 sends the information package or, respectively, the data connection call set-up command in an SMS-type short message format to an appropriate international exchange 5.

310) and 31 1) The international exchange 5 sends the information package or, respectively, the data connection call set-up command in an SMS-type short message format via the international digital telephone network 4 to the foreign mobile phone network operator's international exchange
312) The international exchange 5 the information package or, respectively, the data connection call set-up command in an SMS-type short message format to a foreign operator's MSC 2a.

313) The MSC 2a sends the information package or, respectively, the data connection call set-up command in an SMS-type short message format to the mobile terminal subscription 1. If the information package is already coded in WML, it will be displayed in a suitable manner on the mobile terminal 1.
When the mobile terminal 1 receives a data connection call set-up command, it will establish a data connection call in the manner instructed by the data communication call set-up command.

314) - 320) After the receipt of the data connection call set-up command, the mobile terminal subscription 1 establishes a data connection call to the information server 8 as instructed by the data connection call set-
up command. The data connection call is relayed via the MSC 2a, the foreign operator's international exchange 3, the international digital telephone network 4, the national operator's international exchange 5, the national operator's MSC 6 and the gateway server 10. After a successful set-up of the data connection call, the information server 8 transmits the information package via the data connection call to the mobile terminal 1 , wherein the information package coded in WML will be displayed in a suitable manner.

In the context of the present application and, particularly, in the claims thereof, the term information provider refers to a party which is capable of submitting data over an information network to the operator's system or subsystem and/or of offering its system accessible by the operator's system or subsystem for information retrieval. This type of a party can be, e.g., a server or terminal maintained by the customer himself or the like facility closely associated with the customer in the same manner as the server of the customer's corporate body, for instance. The information provider may also be, e.g., a company specialized in submitting a certain kind of information from its server to an information network and/or a mobile phone network. The information provider may also be a body publishing some type of information, e.g., in a public or private information network such as the Internet or an intranet. Furthermore, the information provider accessible by the operator's subsystem may be another subsystem of the operator.

Further in the context of the present application and, particularly, in the claims thereof, the term information service need profile refers to an outline containing details on the type of information and type of information services that are of interest to a customer and/or other details on the customer that can be used as a basis in the determination of the types of information services on which the customer interests are focused.

In the context of the present application and, particularly, in the claims thereof, the term information server refers to a system capable of maintaining information
received from information providers and/or converting the same into a desired format and/or sending the information via a mobile phone network to a customer's mobile terminal. The operation of the information server may be controlled by the network operator and/or the information provider and/or the customer himself.

Further in the context of the present application and, particularly, in the claims thereof, the term information network refers to a system capable of transmitting information from at least one first physical location to another physical location. Particularly in the context of the present application, such information networks include, among others, the Internet, an extranet, an intranet, a public or a private- access telephone or mobile terminal network or, as an example, an ATM network.

In the context of the present application and, particularly, in the claims thereof, the term corporate body refers to a party with which the mobile terminal subscriber is in some manner associated. Such a body may be, e.g., a firm, association or an organization governed by an authority. The corporate body may modify the information flow of its employee, member or customer in the same fashion as is illustrated in FIG. 2 in regard to the information service provider.
Should the gateway server 10 in the future become capable of performing an HTML-
WML conversion, it is possible that the information server 8 transmits the information package in HTML-format to the gateway server 10.

The WAP-compatible mobile terminal subscription 1 may also be such that is embed- ded in a stationary or mobile machine, automated apparatus or system which is capable of utilizing the received information. A machine compatible with this definition is, e.g., a car that on its vehicle computer receives weather or traffic information transmitted using the method according to the invention.

In addition to GSM networks, the invention can be applied on GPRS (General Packet Radio System), EDGE (Enhanced Data for GSM) and UTMS technologies, since the WAP can used as a protocol between the different transmission paths and connection
technologys. In the above exemplifying embodiments, the application of the invention is described by way of example based generally on the GSM network technology. To a person skilled in the art, however, it is obvious from the above examples and common practice how to apply the invention, e.g., in conjunction with UMTS and GPRS networks. It is also obvious to a person skilled in the art how to replace the network elements described above by the respective elements of the actually used network. It is further obvious to a person skilled in the art that a telephone number as a numeric network address can be replaced by other types of addresses and that the fixed-bandwidth data connection of the GSM network can be replaced by a packet-switched data connection.

In the method according to the invention, the information transmitted over a data connection call can be converted from one form of the WAP-compatible convention to another form of the WAP-compatible convention so that, e.g., the gateway server 10 receives the data in ASCII-WML format and retransmits the same to the mobile phone network in binary WML format. Hence, in the method the format of the data transmitted over a data connection call may be converted from one WML format to another format within the mobile phone network and then the data may again be converted from the other format back a WML format prior to submitting the data to the terminal device.

claim.claim-text: What is claimed is:
1. Method for an information service provided to a mobile terminal subscriber, whereby in the method the following steps are carried out:

- an information need profile is generated for a single customer or group of customers on the basis of information gathered and/or receivedcollected a priori in regard to said customer or associated group of customers,
- pieces of information are received and/or gathered from different sources,
- on the basis of the information need profile, the desired information is selected for the customer or for the group of customers from the received and/or gathered information, and
- said selected information is transmitted (313) to the customer, onto a mobile terminal operating in conjunction with the customer's mobile terminal subscription (1),
characterized in that, to implement said transmission of information,
- a short message containing a data connection call set-up command is sent to said mobile terminal subscription (1),
- a request for establishing a data connection is received from the mobile terminal subscription (1) and a data connection is established, and
- information is sent to the mobile terminal subscription (1) over the established data connection.

2. Method according to claim 1, characterized in that the data connection used in the transmission of said selected information is a fixed-bandwidth data connection
such as a GSM data connection call.

3. Method according to claim 1, characterized in that the data connection used in the transmission of said selected information is a packet-switched data connection such as a GPRS or UMTS network data transfer connection.

4. Method according to any one of claims 1-3, characterized in that data is sent (301 - 302) from an information provider's system (15) and/or systems over an information network to a mobile phone network operator's system and/or the data is stored in said mobile phone network operator's system.

5. Method according to any one of claims 1-4, characterized in that the data is converted (303) in said mobile phone network operator's system, if not already provided in such a format, into a format which is supported in a compatible manner by the customer's mobile terminal and/or the data, which is to be sent over the mobile phone network to a mobile terminal operating in conjunction with the customer's mobile terminal subscription (1), is selected on the basis of a customer- specific information need profile stored in said mobile phone network operator's system.
